# Tasq

The project tracker you share with your agents.

If you run several coding agents on one project - across worktrees, in
parallel sessions, or as a fleet - they duplicate work, overwrite each other's
progress, and forget what happened between sessions. The usual answer is a
hand-maintained PLAN.md or TODO.md, which drifts the moment two of them touch
it. Tasq is the durable version of that file: one SQLite ledger you own, shared
by you and every agent you point at it.

What it gives agents that a scratchpad cannot:

- Exclusive, expiring claims, so two agents never start the same task and
  nobody closes work another is holding.
- Persistent memory of the work itself: a replacement agent resumes from the
  ledger instead of replaying your chat history.
- Evidence-backed completion, so a successful run is never mistaken for a
  finished outcome.
- A way to report what it found - a bug, a missing capability, an
  inconsistency - linked to the task that surfaced it, without losing its claim.

Local-first. One file you own. No account, no cloud, no telemetry.

Try it without installing:
  npx @tasq-run/cli demo

Current boundary: Tasq Local 0.4.2 is published for macOS ARM64 and Linux x64
GNU. Local actors coordinate only when they share the same store and exact
space. Tasq Server, remote MCP and the remote TypeScript, CLI and Python
clients are published and certified. Managed Tasq Cloud is not available, and
remote effects remain disabled.

Agent instructions: https://tasq.run/SKILL.md
Human setup: https://tasq.run/docs/getting-started/
Agent integrations: https://tasq.run/agents/
Machine acquisition: https://tasq.run/adopt.json
Machine integration: https://tasq.run/integration.json
Product truth: https://tasq.run/product-truth.json
